passage:
For his sister's birthday, Paul bought a puzzle. He thought she liked puzzles because she had many in her room.
When she opened the gift, she smiled politely but did not look excited. Later, Paul learned that the puzzles belonged to their cousin. His sister had only been keeping them for a week.
Paul felt bad. His sister said, "It is okay. You tried."
The next day, Paul asked her what she really liked. She said she wanted colored pens. Paul saved money and bought a small set later.
He learned that choosing a gift is not just guessing from what you see. It is paying attention, asking questions, and knowing the person better.
